      "claim": "Step 1 of the Problem section enumerates `_parse_or_reprompt`'s parameters as 'the first turn's result, the caller's parse step as a callable, and the system prompt, turn bound, ceiling, agent and emit'. None of these is `container`, yet the helper is also said to own 'the second turn's ... call' — and every existing `agent` callable in this file is invoked as `agent(container, prompt=..., options=..., ...)`, with `container` a required positional argument supplied by the caller (see `run_lens`'s and `run_wrong_versions`' own first-turn calls, and every test's `agent` double, e.g. `_lens_agent`'s and `_probe_agent`'s `def run(container, *, prompt, options, **kwargs)`). `AttemptResult` (the 'first turn's result') carries no container field either. So the helper as enumerated has no way to supply `container` to the retry's `agent(...)` call. This is resolvable (pass `container` explicitly, or have each caller hand the helper an `agent` already bound to its own `container` via `functools.partial`), and no acceptance witness pins the exact signature, so a cell can still satisfy every acceptance criterion — but the prose itself does not say which resolution it wants, and a person should settle that before the cell starts.",
